reasoning_content:
`serve:instance` is a configuration, not a separate target. The command executed is:

```
nx run urboards:serve:instance --port=38377 --host=0.0.0.0 --allowedHosts=boards.workspace.localhost
```

This ran "successfully" (NX reported success), but the process exited with code 0 right away. The Angular dev server with `--watch=false` exits after building — this is the same pattern as the devcontainer postAttach, `pnpm run build:all && pnpm run start:api-prod-proxy:external`.

Hmm, wait. The dev-server with watch=false builds once and exits. That's why the exit code is 0. But then who actually serves the app? Let me look at the `instance` build target — maybe it builds to a dist directory that nginx/proxy serves statically.

Looking at the proxy's nginx configuration — the shared proxy (urbo-proxy) serves the app. Maybe the dev server just builds into a directory, and nginx serves the static files. Let me check render.mjs/nginx.conf to see how app.workspace.localhost is served.

action.command: cd /workspace && grep -n "app\.\|cms\.\|boards\." .urbo/workspace/nginx.conf | head -20; echo "=== upstreams ==="; grep -n "upstream\|proxy_pass" .urbo/workspace/nginx.conf | head -20
